findings.actual: shape-only validation did not prove that provider metadata was safe to retain

findings.reproduction: run the CLI repeatedly with --live; the in-memory hash ledger resets per process
findings.actual: hard maximum 50 and duplicate-request blocking apply per invocation; cumulative usage is not persisted
findings.action: default to one call, require explicit budget for larger runs, and manually track cumulative approved spend

findings.reproduction: import JevClient directly and supply an arbitrary approved_request_hashes set
findings.expected: a reusable client would enforce its own trusted dataset boundary
findings.actual: synthetic-only restriction is enforced by the CLI loader; the client accepts caller-supplied hashes
findings.action: keep this harness isolated and do not treat JevClient as a generic security boundary

recommendation: Keep the prototype isolated. The Polza System One request/response path worked once, but Jev quality on Russian business news is NOT MEASURED. Do not rely on it or integrate it into the runtime until an independently adjudicated benchmark and an explicitly budgeted evaluation support that decision.
